source.title: STEVE: A Step Verification Pipeline for Computer-use Agent Training
source.authors: Fanbin Lu; Zhisheng Zhong; Ziqin Wei; Shu Liu; Chi-Wing Fu; Jiaya Jia

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports downstream task success across iterative KTO training rounds and with increased trajectory collection, a different measure and setup from the original held-out-loss scaling studies. This bears only on V6.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions data scaling laws as motivation, but does not measure held-out cross-entropy or sweep model parameters, training tokens, or compute. Its agent task-success results across KTO rounds bear on V6; results on UI grounding benchmarks and other comparisons do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites data scaling laws only as motivation. It reports its own KTO agent's task success over training rounds, with no loss, no parameter/token/compute sweep and no fitted law. That is the method's own performance, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors say KTO with GPT-4o step verification beats SFT, keeps UI localization, and improves as more trajectories are collected. They frame this as the pipeline's scalability, not as a scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses KTO with GPT-4o-verified computer-use trajectories and evaluates task success across training rounds; it does not fit held-out-loss scaling laws or test parameter/token/compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Task success is reported by WinAgentArena domain and KTO round; no other setting sensitivity relevant to the loss-scaling claim is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: KTO agent task success on WinAgentArena splits rises over three trajectory-collection rounds (R3: 46%, 26%, 18%). Fig. 1 shows the KTO agent beating SFT as computer-use time increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agent fine-tuning performance improves with more step-verified trajectory data (no fitted law).

record.problems: No held-out loss or scaling-law fit is reported. The multi-round evidence is limited to a 7B agent and task-success rates; exact R1 and R2 values are not stated in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are given for the reported averages.

untested.parts: No held-out loss, no parameter/token/compute sweep.
No power-law loss fit in any regime, including fine-tuning.
No downstream performance measured against pretraining scale or loss. Only a single 7B model is used.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link and 'supports' label are removed. Improvement across fine-tuning rounds of one 7B model is the study's own method performance. It is not downstream predictability from pretraining scale or loss. 'Data scaling law' appears only as motivation in the abstract.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or parameter, token, or compute scaling sweep.
No fitting on small runs or extrapolation to larger runs.
No compute-budget allocation sweep over parameters and tokens.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law loss scaling in another modality or training regime.
Tests task success across KTO trajectory-collection rounds in a computer-use setting, but not a fitted predictive relationship, pretraining loss, or scaling across model sizes.
No comparison of loss exponents or fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from a power law.

reader_labels.condition: 7B KTO agent across the tested WinAgentArena File Explorer, Web Browser, and VsCode splits
reader_labels.reason: The authors report increasing task success across KTO rounds as trajectory collection grows, with R3 rates of 46%, 26%, and 18%, respectively (r3, r6, r9, r10). This supports an improvement trend in this setting, not a fitted prediction law.
